title: Design a Next.js backend-for-frontend with bounded ownership
businessContext: One Route Handler proxies arbitrary user URLs with server credentials and buffers unlimited responses.
problemStatement: Design the system for Web UI plus mobile/external consumers; three upstream services. Produce the component/data-flow diagram, request and mutation contracts, cache/trust boundaries, capacity assumptions, failure recovery and rollout gates. State which decisions change between Next.js 15 and 16 instead of using a framework API as a substitute for an architectural guarantee.
constraints: Expose an explicit admitted API surface.
Bound work and separate public consumer contracts from UI composition.
candidateTasks: Draw components and annotate ownership of data, identity, caches and durable work.
Specify contracts/schema and quantify the capacity/freshness assumptions.
Walk through the failure scenario and design measurable acceptance tests.
Compare the reference decisions and answer the changed-requirement interview prompt.

systemDesignReqs.scale: Web UI plus mobile/external consumers; three upstream services
functional: Expose an explicit admitted API surface.
Bound work and separate public consumer contracts from UI composition.
nonFunctional: State an explicit latency, freshness and recovery budget rather than inventing guarantees.
Keep actor/tenant isolation and failure ownership observable.
assumptions: A patched App Router deployment; platform-specific infrastructure support must be verified.
Next.js version and Cache Components configuration are explicit design inputs.

hints: Use server-owned upstream destinations, validated DTOs, per-operation authorization and explicit timeouts/body limits.

A client-supplied destination can become SSRF or credential exfiltration. Reject arbitrary hosts/redirect chains, constrain egress at the infrastructure layer, and avoid forwarding authentication headers to untrusted origins.
alternativeApproaches: Prefer a documented stable application API for external clients. Framework transport is not a general version-independent public business contract; separate that boundary from internal UI rendering.
commonMistakes: Claiming a cache API provides transactions, durable delivery or cross-region consistency.
Omitting authorization, recovery budgets or evidence from an otherwise attractive component diagram.

verification: Test malformed, oversized and unauthorized requests.
Inject stalls, partial bodies and non-JSON upstream failures.
Prove no credential crosses an unauthorized host or appears in client errors.
nextjsPractice.next15: Use patched Next.js 15 and the router family named by the file path. Await request APIs where the App Router contract requires it; validate behavior in a production build.
nextjsPractice.next16: Applies to Next.js 16.4.5. Cache Components is disabled unless the exercise explicitly enables it. The simulator itself remains on 16.4.3.
